set_aside.subject: reach_operation_element
set_aside.text: - reach_operation_element: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST run in this order: check_binding_current for the binding; a StaleBinding writes RecordOperationFailureChange with status operation_failed and detail binding_stale; then reads every input's bytes with read_value_bytes, a value port as JsonPayload of its one StoredValue's canonical bytes and a file port as FilePayload, or FileListPayload in list order for a many port, and calls prepare_request with the current operation, the instance_name the check returned, the binding's input and output ports and those payloads; a PreSendFailure writes RecordOperationFailureChange with status operation_failed and that failure's detail_code and reason as failure_detail; then for a non-read binding asks find_send_authority with the prepared request_digest, and when it finds none requests the approval as its note below says and sends nothing; otherwise calls send_under_authority with the run, the element, the given inputs, the binding, the prepared request, the authority found (None for a read binding) and the actor.
set_aside.other_text: - PortRef discriminated union on field 'ref_kind' (exact variants, no others exist): StoredValuesRef (ref_kind='stored_values'), SpooledFilesRef (ref_kind='spooled_files'), FileFactsRef (ref_kind='file_facts'); a value of PortRef is an instance of one of these variants, never of another model, and PortRef itself is not constructed
set_aside.question: Must FileFactsRef be excluded from reach_operation_element inputs, must ByteSource gain a source capable of reading FileFactsRef content, or must the requirement stop requiring every PortRef input's bytes to be read?
set_aside.set_aside_because: an unchanged passage of a unit reviewed for its change

set_aside.subject: send_under_authority
set_aside.text: - send_under_authority: [BEHAVIOR] When the SendResult outcome is succeeded MUST store the outputs before writing: each JSON output whose canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant turns the outcome into contract_violation with detail value_too_large and no outputs; otherwise each JSON output is published with put_value_bytes — its value_digest is content_identity of a BytesContent holding the bytes and value_id content_identity of the StoredValueContent — and becomes a StoredValue of value carriage with the output port's stored schema (M21: its value_schema, or for a many port the canonical array schema with it as items), its size and the class the binding declares for that port, and a file output is published with spool_file under SpooledFileKey of the run, node, map_index, this attempt_number, the port and no list_index, becoming a SpooledFile of the port's declared class, which every port of a binding has, since a proposal leaving out a port's class is refused (A08 rule 5, M01), so that class is always a DisclosureClass member; a RefusedError from spool_file turns the outcome into contract_violation with no outputs, a non-read binding's attempt still applied (a read binding has no attempt).
set_aside.other_text: - PortPayload discriminated union on field 'payload_kind' (exact variants, no others exist): JsonPayload (payload_kind='json'), FilePayload (payload_kind='file'), FileListPayload (payload_kind='file_list'); a value of PortPayload is an instance of one of these variants, never of another model, and PortPayload itself is not constructed
set_aside.question: For a FileListPayload, must each contained file be spooled with a distinct list_index, must FileListPayload be excluded from SendResult outputs, or must the requirement that every file output use no list_index change?
set_aside.set_aside_because: an unchanged passage of a unit reviewed for its change
